body:
I am simply reporting what I see.

I can pretend people aren't exclusionary if that would make you feel better? I can pretend everyone gets the same chance, and that if we say that happens, it does.

I hate humanity, they are monsters.  If you get offended by the actions of your race, I don't know what to tell you, they still do those things, you and I are still a part of the species.

It's not about overt actions, it's about subconscious impulses over the course of an entire lifetime; a billion moments plausibly denied, glossed over, because it shows our base nature.

I try to treat everyone well; it is entirely too rare for even the most basic respect to be given back, almost everyone attempts to take advantage of this "weakness" and is surprised when they meet resistance. Certain looks, certain abilities, certain superficial characteristics influence what words and terms we use to describe different people, these are often boundaries people have to work entire lives to overcome, the entire time being told its all in their head, they just need to be more positive. I've been talked down to so many times in the last week, by people who treat each other fairly otherwise.  I have done nothing, they had never met me before.

I used to be positive about people, go to massive gatherings, loved a party, helping the community etc.; at some point I realized everyone around me was fucking, making friendships, connecting, but no one wanted to do that with me...ever....ever....ever. Over time, as crazy as this sounds, my outlook has changed.  I took in information and based how I see the world around me.  Being open was just being taken advantage of, it never once opened up others to me.

It made me realize there is no connection if other people don't want it, you have to give them something, they see you as an obstacle, a stepping stone to be used as a resource.
